Moodle MCP for ChatGPT

Give teachers and students a course-level connection between their own ChatGPT account and the Moodle content and tools they are allowed to access.

The block makes the course MCP connection visible where learning happens. It works with local_mcp, respects each person's Moodle identity and can expose study information or carefully scoped teaching tools without relying on shared credentials.

Course-level capabilities
  • Personal ChatGPT connections using each user's Moodle account.
  • Study access to visible content, tasks and the learner's own grades.
  • Audience controls for teachers or teachers and students.
  • Optional, allowlisted teacher write tools disabled by default.
Personal study assistant
Learners can ask about accessible course materials, their upcoming tasks and grades they are permitted to see, without opening up other users' records.
Teacher-oriented tools
Educators can inspect course context and, when explicitly enabled and authorized, use a restricted set of course-management operations.
Permission-aware access
Course visibility, enrolment, block configuration and Moodle capabilities are checked again when tools execute; administrative operations remain outside educational access.
An AI connection that belongs to the user

A shared integration token is a poor fit for education because it cannot reliably represent the different permissions of a student, a teacher and an administrator. Moodle MCP for ChatGPT connects through each person's own Moodle account, while local_mcp provides the underlying protocol and authorization services.

The current 1.0.1 beta depends on educational OAuth support in local_mcp; the block's repository documents an accompanying authorization integration patch that is required for teacher and student connections. Custom MCP connections must also be supported by the user's ChatGPT account or workspace.
